[TEST FIXTURE] Spinel LiMn2O4 electrodes in aqueous LiCl

 Abstract
This fixture abstract describes LiMn2O4 composite electrodes cycled in 1 M LiCl aqueous electrolyte. Cyclic voltammetry at 1 mV s−1 versus Ag/AgCl showed two pairs of redox peaks. When the upper potential exceeded 1.1 V, oxygen evolution occurred as a side reaction and the coulombic efficiency decreased. The fixture text exists only for unit tests and is long enough to be treated as an abstract by the parser.

Electrodes were prepared from LiMn2O4, carbon black and PVDF. Measurements used a Pt counter electrode and an Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode.

 3. Results and discussion
Manganese dissolution into the electrolyte was detected after cycling, consistent with capacity fading over repeated cycles. Dissolution increased when the electrode was held at high potential.

Avoiding potentials above 1.1 V limited oxygen evolution.

## 2. Experimental
Electrodes were prepared from LiMn2O4, carbon black and PVDF. Measurements used a Pt counter electrode and an Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode.

## 3. Results and discussion
Manganese dissolution into the electrolyte was detected after cycling, consistent with capacity fading over repeated cycles. Dissolution increased when the electrode was held at high potential.

## 4. Conclusions
Avoiding potentials above 1.1 V limited oxygen evolution.
